title: "It's a dark comet": UFO expert breaks down the mystery surrounding space object 1998 KY26
excerpt: UFO expert and Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb explained the mystery surrounding the space object named 1998 KY26 while speaking to Fox Weather's Melanie Black and Michael Estime.
content:
UFO expert and Harvard astrophysicist Avi Loeb explained the mystery surrounding the space object named 1998 KY26 while speaking to Fox Weather's Melanie Black and Michael Estime. Loeb said,

"Well, comet experts argue that it's a dark comet because there is a non-gravitational force acting on it, something that is not gravity that is pushing it, and they don't see any gas or dust coming off it. So they say it's a comet, but we can't see any signs of a comet, so it's a dark comet."

Loeb further explained that researchers noticed the object traveling along the same path as Phobos 1, which was a Soviet space mission lost in 1988. The expert also pointed out that the object was highly reflective, bouncing back nearly half of the sunlight that struck its surface. According to Loeb, the object was roughly 10 meters in size, comparable in scale to the Phobos 1 spacecraft.

Continue reading more about the story.

UFO updates: Avi Loeb decoded the secrets surrounding near-Earth object 1998 KY26

While speaking to Fox Weather's reporters Melanie Black and Michael Estime, the UFO expert explained that some comet experts believe the object was a 'dark comet' because it appeared to be influenced by a non-gravitational force.

The UFO expert further mentioned that researchers have not detected any gas or dust being released from the object, which are usually signs of a comet. Consequently, it had been classified as a 'dark comet' despite the lack of visible comet-like activity. Loeb added that the object also followed the same trajectory as Phobos 1.

According to the study, asteroid 1998 KY26 measures about 36 feet across, although estimates suggested it could be as large as 43 feet. The researchers also found that the asteroid rotates at an exceptionally high speed and completes one full spin every 5.35 minutes.

Data from the European Space Agency's (ESA) asteroid database revealed that it took 498 Earth days to complete a single orbit around the Sun. ESA also reported that the asteroid's next close approach to Earth is expected in May 2039, when it will pass at a distance of roughly 10.1 million miles.

Loeb revealed Oumuamua might be from an alien space agency

The UFO expert explained that scientists had monitored the object intermittently, but a new mission was planned to visit it and gather more information because it was classified as a dark comet. He said the dark comet concept was developed after the discovery of an interstellar object known as Oumuamua in 2017. Loeb stated:

"The reason the dark comet concept was invented is another visit by an object from outside the solar system, called Oumuamua, that was discovered in 2017 and again showed non-gravitational acceleration without any outgassing, no gas or dust around it."

Loeb detailed that Oumuamua showed non-gravitational acceleration even though researchers detected no outgassing and found no surrounding gas or dust, which led scientists to introduce the dark comet idea.

Loeb also revealed that Oumuamua might have been launched by an alien space agency from another solar system. Referring to both Oumuamua and Hayabusa 2 (an asteroid sample-return mission), he suggested that these objects could have been propelled by energy from the Sun.
